scope: Fix every finding in the referenced project review; completion requires current evidence for each item

items.requirement: Keep provider secrets in backend; scoped expiring runtime LLM tokens, allowed model and quotas
evidence: Runtime receives only a model-only JWT; provider key stays in independent llm-gateway process. Hash persistence reuses revocable runtime records.
JWT binds user/workspace/runtime/model and maximum one-hour expiry; gateway checks current runtime state and editor membership, rejects REST/MCP credentials and alternate models.
Body/output/stream caps and atomic shared user/workspace/runtime Redis reservations; text/tool inputs only; no upstream redirect or caller headers.
HTTP forwarding, SSE, errors, expiration/revocation/demotion, cross-endpoint rejection and real Redis concurrency/recreation checks passed.
Complete OpenCode -> gateway -> mock-provider flow using PostgreSQL remains to be exercised alongside controller relay.

items.requirement: Separate runtimes from database, cache, queue and object storage; restrict egress
evidence: Dedicated internal runtime network; API and DB/Redis/MQ/MinIO never join it. Controller relays application traffic from separate control network.
Real tests prove Runtime cannot reach infrastructure by DNS/direct IP, bridge can, and Controller management socket is unreachable from Runtime network even with correct credentials.
No Runtime host port or host volume; production Compose publishes only frontend.

items.requirement: Remove Docker socket from API; authenticated restricted controller
evidence: Standalone authenticated Controller is the sole Docker socket owner. Only fixed pinned image, positive identities, managed labeled containers, internal network and sandbox options are accepted; no caller-selected Docker options or arbitrary exec API.

API uses scoped RPC and bounded authenticated HTTP/SSE relay, leaves runtime network. Controller binds only its separate control-network interface; Runtime cannot reach management API even with its token.

27 targeted Controller/MCP tests and six real Docker/Redis security checks passed. Actual create/start/stop/remove, configuration reload, OpenCode health/session/SSE and unauthorized caller rejection verified.

items.requirement: Reject passwords in profile update; require dedicated password change
evidence: Profile schema forbids extra fields; service permits only username/avatar; dedicated password service retains old-password checks
HTTP regression tests reject password profile mutation and preserve stored credentials

items.requirement: Fail closed on default secrets; explicit administrator bootstrap
evidence: Removed fixed JWT signing-key fallback; missing/short/placeholder secrets fail closed. OpenCode server derivation requires independent configured secret.
Private exclusive env generator creates six independent random secrets, mode 0600; Compose rejects missing infrastructure/Controller credentials.

Removed known-password administrator and fixed-ID personal workspace seeds. Interactive first-admin command creates account/workspace/membership/root in one transaction; PostgreSQL advisory lock prevents concurrent initial administrators.

Startup validates independent signing/controller keys and explicit database, queue and storage passwords (at least 12 characters); adapters reject missing, placeholder and URL-encoded defaults before contacting infrastructure. Known historical seeded administrator is blocked at startup and login; terminal-only reset preserves existing workspace data and atomically revokes sessions/tokens. Deployment regression tests and 10 real PostgreSQL scenarios passed.

items.requirement: Production infrastructure internal; development overrides
evidence: Production compose publishes frontend only. Explicit development override binds all administrative service ports to 127.0.0.1.
MCP accessed via frontend /mcp; frontend endpoint changed to same origin and nginx streaming proxy added.
Production/development compose config checks and actual nginx -t passed; frontend type-check, unit tests and build passed.

items.requirement: Streaming file limits, user/workspace capacity, daily rate, multipart reservations and concurrency
evidence: Positive finite defaults: file 256 MiB, avatar 5 MiB, request 512 MiB, part 64 MiB. Nginx body limit is finite; actual container nginx -t passed. Invalid/zero/negative upload configurations fail closed.

ASGI middleware counts actual request bytes before multipart parsing, handles missing Content-Length, returns 413 and closes already-open multipart spools. HTTP, Base64, and Werkzeug adapters bound writes; Base64 encoded size is checked before decoding. Single/batch/part/assembly paths preserve 413 and clean incomplete temporary files.

Unique temporary names prevent concurrent part writes sharing one temp file; oversized replacement preserves existing part. Preflight and legacy multipart completion obey finite file limits; assembly checks each stored part while copying. New upload behavior tests and full backend unit regression passed.

Durable user/workspace reservations and UTC daily admissions apply to direct/batch/instant/multipart uploads; fixed row lock order serializes user, workspace and daily races. File insertion and reservation consumption commit together; only session creator can resume/read/write/complete/abort. One-hour expiry and minute Worker cleanup hold writer locks. Quotas retain uncertain orphan-object capacity until confirmed deletion. Staging process leases preserve live writers and reclaim actual crashed-process files; object keys are journaled before PUT, referenced objects preserved, failed deletions retried. 16 quota cases, 17 streaming/body cases, 3 staging cases, 14 PostgreSQL scenarios and 5 real PostgreSQL/MinIO HTTP/failure/crash scenarios passed.

MCP inline inputs are rejected before oversized Base64 decode/encode; JSON RPC is bounded before parsing at 32 MiB / 4 concurrent POSTs. REST ingress limits and API process upload concurrency are also bounded. Old unfinished sessions receive explicit reinitialization conflict rather than internal errors.

items.requirement: Remove URL JWT; authenticated downloads and scoped short lived iframe tickets
evidence: REST accepts only Authorization Bearer; signed query JWT and generic cookies are rejected. Downloads and protected Markdown/raw HTML images use authenticated Blob requests; historical URLs are normalized and object URLs released. HTTP and frontend behavior regressions passed, including actual PostgreSQL/MinIO download.
SSE already uses Authorization headers. Scoped iframe tickets and a functioning isolated UI proxy remain pending; existing iframe fallback still needs replacement.

items.requirement: Alembic versioned schema upgrades; startup version check without DDL
evidence: Alembic baseline uses immutable schema SQL snapshot, adopts unversioned databases, repairs known legacy columns; second revision repairs file/chunk cosine vector indexes. No live ORM create_all in migration revisions.

Explicit entry.migrate / standard Alembic upgrade supported. PostgreSQL advisory transaction lock serializes concurrent migration processes, lock timeout bounds waits, all DDL/revision updates roll back atomically on failure. Destructive baseline downgrade is rejected.

Application initialization has no DDL. API, Worker, MCP and model gateway check exact Alembic head before startup; missing/old/future/branched versions rejected. Real application startup passes with read-only database role permitted only SELECT on alembic_version.

Compose removes init SQL mount, adds dedicated migrate service, and starts all four application services only after successful completion. README documents backup, explicit upgrade and recovery requirements.

Seven isolated real PostgreSQL tests passed: fresh model-column/vector compatibility and repeat upgrade; legacy missing-column/wrong-index repair preserving data; failed upgrade rollback; concurrent processes; standard Alembic CLI; read-only startup; version mismatch/destructive downgrade checks. /private/tmp/skycloud-final-real-migrations.log
Revision 0003 adds auth_version; current startup gate matches this head. Updated real migrations suite: 8 passed including concurrent password reset and transaction rollback.

Revision 0004 removes external MCP plaintext credentials and enforces at most one unrevoked token per user; current startup gate is 0004_hash_only_mcp. Nine real PostgreSQL migration scenarios passed.
Head 0005_upload_quotas adds reservation/daily admission tables; fresh model compatibility and all 13 real PostgreSQL migration/transaction scenarios passed.

items.requirement: Invalidate previous web sessions on password change
evidence: Added users.auth_version via versioned migration 0003_auth_version. Login signs version into Web JWT; REST and MCP Web-session validation check authoritative scalar database version, bypassing profile caches and ORM identity state. Missing/noninteger/negative/mismatched versions rejected, unknown scopes denied.

Password changes lock and refresh the account row, validate old password for nonadmins, increment version and revoke external MCP and all Runtime credentials in the same transaction. Administrator reset affects target only.

HTTP regressions prove old sessions rejected after own/admin password changes, new login works, bad old password leaves session usable, stale cache cannot restore revoked session, legacy tokens and malformed versions rejected. Runtime LLM/MCP and external MCP revocation tests passed.

Real PostgreSQL test proves failed commit rolls back password/version/token revocation and simultaneous changes using one old password produce exactly one success. Existing frontend already signs out after successful password change; docs explain migration reauthentication and MCP/Runtime reconfiguration.

items.requirement: Store only token hash; reveal raw token once and update client flow
evidence: Removed token_value from ORM and persistence. All external MCP tokens store only SHA-256 hashes and hash-derived fingerprints; even short compatibility credentials cannot leak through previews.

GET /auth/mcp-token returns metadata only, does not issue a credential; login/registration no longer auto-issue discarded external MCP tokens. POST refresh reveals the new raw credential once and sends Cache-Control: no-store.
Migration 0004 rotates historical credentials, drops plaintext column and adds partial unique index on active user token. Issuance locks owner row to serialize concurrent refreshes.

Frontend consumes separate read/issuance contracts, displays raw credential only in current modal session; closes/unmounts clear memory, reopening reads metadata only, late responses are discarded and duplicate issuance blocked. Four frontend behavior tests passed; full frontend tests 9 passed, type-check and build passed.

Real Redis + SQLite auth suite: 67 passed. Full backend unit suite: 1187 passed, zero failures. Final real PostgreSQL suite: 9 passed, including legacy credential revocation/plaintext-column removal and concurrent issuance leaving exactly one valid credential.

items.requirement: Non-root runtime, drop capabilities, no privilege escalation, PID and disk limits

Bounded tmpfs: home 256 MiB, workspace 512 MiB, /tmp 64 MiB. No host volume or Docker socket supplied to runtime.
Pinned installed upstream image digest, --pure mode avoids external plugins, provider/agent config reloads via instance/dispose instead of container restart.
Real unmocked Docker SDK integration verified running UID, forbidden rootfs write, applied resource policy, authenticated health and successful config reload with retained model/credential.
